introduction: This foundational level introduces the scope of Hindu Law in India. It defines who is considered a 'Hindu' under the law, identifies the ancient and modern sources of Hindu law, and breaks down the strict legal conditions required for a valid Hindu marriage under the Hindu Marriage Act (HMA), 1955.

core_concepts.title: Application: Who is a Hindu? (Section 2, HMA)
core_concepts.description:
Hindu Law applies to any person who is a Hindu by religion (including Virashaiva, Lingayat, Brahmo, Prarthana, or Arya Samaj followers). 
- Crucial Inclusion: It also applies to Buddhists, Jains, and Sikhs by religion.
- Exclusion: It does NOT apply to Muslims, Christians, Parsis, or Jews. Any person who is not a Muslim, Christian, Parsi, or Jew is presumed to be governed by Hindu law unless proven otherwise.

core_concepts.title: Sources of Hindu Law
core_concepts.description:
1. Ancient Sources: Shruti (what was heard/Vedas), Smriti (what was remembered/Dharmashastras like Manusmriti), Commentaries/Digests (Mitakshara and Dayabhaga), and Custom (the most powerful ancient source).
2. Modern Sources: Judicial Precedents (Supreme Court/High Court decisions), Legislation (Codified acts like HMA 1955, HSA 1956), and Justice, Equity, and Good Conscience.

core_concepts.title: Conditions for a Valid Marriage (Section 5, HMA)
core_concepts.description:
For a Hindu marriage to be legally valid, it must fulfill these 5 conditions:
1. Monogamy: Neither party has a spouse living at the time of marriage.
2. Mental Capacity: Neither party is incapable of giving valid consent due to unsoundness of mind, mental disorder, or insanity.
3. Age: The bridegroom has completed 21 years, and the bride 18 years.
4. Prohibited Degrees: The parties are not within the degrees of prohibited relationship (unless custom permits).
5. Sapinda: The parties are not 'Sapindas' of each other (unless custom permits).

core_concepts.title: Ceremonies of Hindu Marriage (Section 7, HMA)
core_concepts.description:
A Hindu marriage may be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites of either party. 
- Saptapadi: Where the rites include the 'Saptapadi' (taking seven steps jointly before the sacred fire), the marriage becomes complete and binding immediately upon the taking of the seventh step.

important_entities.name: Custom Overriding Text
important_entities.key_fact: A valid custom outweighs written Hindu Law texts.
important_entities.significance: In Hindu Law, clear proof of usage (custom) will outweigh the written text of the law. For example, marrying within prohibited degrees or Sapinda relationships is normally void, BUT if a proven local or family custom (like South Indian cross-cousin marriages) allows it, the marriage is perfectly valid.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A highly tested exam trap. If A (19-year-old male) marries B (16-year-old female), is the marriage Void or Voidable under the Hindu Marriage Act? **NEITHER**. Violation of the age condition (Sec 5(iii)) makes the marriage punishable, but it remains a VALID marriage under the HMA. It does not fall under Void (Sec 11) or Voidable (Sec 12) provisions of HMA. (Note: The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 deals with annulment separately).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: M A M P S (Monogamy, Age, Mental capacity, Prohibited degrees, Sapinda)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use MAMPS to remember the 5 pillars of a valid Hindu marriage.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a Judiciary question asks 'To whom does the Hindu Marriage Act apply?', remember to explicitly select the option that includes **Buddhists, Jains, and Sikhs**.
